coding with agents is expensive. At Pedal, we use Claude for almost everything, and it's been a constant challenge to manage cost without interrupting my work.

  • i hit session token limits
  • i hit weekly and monthly spend caps
  • i switch models, accounts and credit cards to make sure i don't run out while im working on something important.

This week, i did an analysis and found that a lot of the things i use my budget on are....not really client facing. they're barely even coding--its cleanup, QA, reminders, and documentation. almost all of it is rote, repeated, and (to be frank) quite mundane.

So, I designed a game for my agents to play to incentivize using free, open source models instead of relying solely on cheaper Anthropic models.

Two chores moved from paid Claude calls to a free model running on my own machine (qwen3-coder:30b): sorting my inboxes and labeling GitHub issues. Aggregates only: counts, dollars and milliseconds, never a message, sender or issue.
